title: A caller transaction with more than about 1,000 row writes to a table escalates to a table lock; every other process's write to that table, in any graph, then waits 10 s and fails with SQLCODE -110
intended: No IVG document states whether one graph's (or tenant's) transaction may block writes to other graphs: a search of docs/, specs/ and README.md at the pin for lock escalation, LockThreshold or escalat* finds no statement on it; the multi-graph documents promise isolation of answers (SYS-I2), not of availability. The product neither documents nor configures the IRIS lock-escalation threshold (the engine default; iris-contract treats lock escalation as an engine feature). Intent undecided.
observed: Live on AUDITD (structural lane, st-live-cap-batch, part '03 lock escalation'): with setAutoCommit(False), a caller transaction holding 200 create_node inserts leaves row locks only, and a second process's create_node succeeds in 0.03 s; holding 1,500 inserts, the lock table shows table locks ^t52S.XCFT.1 (nodes) and ^t52S.DMCe.1 (rdf_props) in mode X, and a second process's create_node of another node in another call waits 10.09 s and raises GraphWriteError SQLCODE -110 'nothing written' (its node is absent and the answer is consistent). Answers stay consistent; only availability across graphs is affected.
remedy: Decide whether large caller transactions may block other graphs' writers; if not, document a batch limit below the escalation threshold or configure the threshold for IVG's tables, and say so in the operations guide.
notes: Filed by the orchestrator from the structural lane's observation (the lane recorded it as intent-undecided without a finding). The st-live-cap-batch record is 'incomplete' overall because its Cypher UNWIND part was undecided (rerun as st-live-cap-batch-r2); the escalation part is decided in its log.

title: When its dedicated Native API connection is refused (licence units exhausted), the engine silently uses the caller's connection and retries the refused connect on every native call
intended: iris_vector_graph/engine.py:1895-1898: the dedicated connection exists because mixing iris.createIRIS() and cursor DDL on the same connection 'permanently corrupts the IRIS Python driver's parameter binding state'; :1913-1918: the caller's connection is used only 'when [the credentials] are not known'. The product's convention against swallowed failures (C-17, product-gates/STYLE.md) asks that a failed step be reported.
observed: Live (live-licence-world, AUDITE, IRIS Community 2026.1, 8 licence units): an engine from IRISGraphEngine.from_connect, then 7 idle connections taking every free unit (the 8th refused 'Unable to allocate a license'); the engine's first native call (ledger enable/commit) could not open its dedicated connection; engine._native_conn stayed None and the calls ran on the caller's own connection (engine.py:1940-1941, except Exception: return _create(self.conn)), with no warning or error logged. Each later native call tried the refused connect again: two 150- and 3-operation commits took 2,062.6 ms and 2,017.0 ms against 47.3 ms and 1.46 ms with units free (control world C, registered run r2; an earlier failed harness attempt r1 showed 209 ms and 1.6 ms for the control). The commits stayed all-or-nothing, parameterised reads stayed correct and verify() was equal in this sequence; the driver-state corruption the comment names was not observed. With units exhausted before connecting, from_connect raised the licence error and nothing was written.
remedy: Log the refused dedicated connect and either raise or record the degraded mode once (do not retry the connect on every native call); if sharing the caller's connection is unsafe, as the comment says, refuse instead of falling back.
notes: Failure scenario S6 (licence refusal at product level), run by the orchestrator while no lane used the container; the style lane had read the same lines as a borderline C-17 case from source. Its id (nn 95) lies in the product-gates lane's range; the orchestrator filed it, after that lane had finished.

title: A refused Eraser probe is cached as 'absent': the store's deletes then run as plain SQL and leave the ledger statements of the deleted edges live
intended: iris_vector_graph/stores/iris_sql_store.py:1333-1338 (delete_nodes' docstring reserves the SQL path for 'an install with no ObjectScript classes, hence no ^KG to maintain'; here the classes, the ledger and ^KG all exist); INV-stmt / ERS-I2 (no live statement without its row, experiment/playbook-uplift/ontology/12-erasure.md:42). Context, not the anchor: docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:511-514's ClassesUnreadable rule covers only a routines database the role cannot read (raised when the <PROTECT> names that database, iris_vector_graph/schema.py:119-143); for a refusal that names no database, a missing %Native_ClassExecution, the pin makes the opposite choice and lets 'absent' stand (schema.py:134-137; the engine's capability probe likewise, at DEBUG, schema.py:2828-2830). R206 (_dictionary.py:8-12) fixed the refused dictionary SELECT by asking natively and says nothing about a refused native call.
observed: Live in AUDITB (ws-live-sql-fallback-priv), as the operator-authorised disposable principal, ledger enabled (not strict), 4 nodes and 2 recorded edges, verify() equal. With ADMIN_GUIDE's writing row (%DB_%DEFAULT:RW, %Native_ClassExecution:U, %Native_GlobalAccess:U, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE ON SCHEMA Graph_KG) engine.delete_node('sfp|a') and IRISGraphStore.delete_edges([('sfp|c','R','sfp|d')]) went through Graph.KG.Eraser (probe cache True) and the rows, the ^KG out entries and both ledger statements went. With the same role without %Native_ClassExecution the probe's native IDKEYExists raised '<PROTECT> *Resource %Native_ClassExecution required' (the run's DEBUG line 'Graph.KG.Eraser.EraseNodeIds taken as absent: ...'; that the dictionary SELECT was refused with -99 before it is read from _dictionary.py:48-56, not logged), and _has_eraser_method (iris_sql_store.py:1307-1318, except Exception -> False, cached for the store's life) took the Eraser as absent, logged at DEBUG only; both calls returned success through the SQL fallbacks (_delete_nodes_sql, iris_sql_store.py:1363-1418; delete_edges, :1504-1518), which deleted the rows and left both statements (^IVG.Ledger tuple and stmt, closed seq empty) live without their rows. No warning or error was raised. Any other exception of the probe (a transient driver or network error) takes the same path for the life of that store.
remedy: Treat only a definite 'not compiled' answer as absent: re-raise (or raise ClassesUnreadable) on a refusal or any other probe error, do not cache a failed probe, and log the fallback at WARNING; or remove the SQL fallback for namespaces where the ledger or ^KG exists.
notes: Filed by the orchestrator from the writer census (WS-OBL-147/148/150/154 were open as 'unreached at the pin's deploy'); id in the writesets lane's range (nn 50-69), that lane having finished. The role without %Native_ClassExecution departs from ADMIN_GUIDE's writing row; the defect is the silent fallback into a path the code reserves for installs without the classes, which breaks INV-stmt and reports success; any other probe exception (a transient driver or network error) takes the same path with no unusual role. Maintainer question: must a role without %Native_ClassExecution be refused, or served (the pin serves it elsewhere, schema.py:134-137), and if served, may the store's deletes fall back to SQL while the ledger and ^KG exist? Same pattern as the ledger guard's fail-open (F-0801) and the engine's native fallback (F-C1795). The five 'gref ... Returning a mock object' WARNING lines in each variant's log are emitted by the driver package's embedded-python shim (_iris_ep/_runtime_facade.py) on a lookup of iris.gref outside embedded Python; they appear identically with both roles and say nothing about the fallback.
